title: The environment kinds are fenced BEFORE they exist: MCP-excluded and human-only
description:
Prerequisite LEAF carved out of task-a2409cba9ad841a690961692a2948c41 by worker-caece97b (acting as architect on a claimed PLANNING row), 2026-09-05, because a2409cba measured 13 forced file edits against the 10-file hard cap and its obvious seam turned out to be WELDED SHUT. Parent chain: SPIDR child 1b of task-9ae492b373fa4e7aa6b1e91585f6e612.

WHY THE OBVIOUS SPLIT IS IMPOSSIBLE, so nobody re-proposes it. `apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:238` asserts SET-EQUALITY between the v2 command plane's registry keys and `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` (minus the one named `planning.submit_decomposition` exception):

    expect([...v2.registry.keys()].sort()).toEqual(Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)
      .filter((kind) => kind !== "planning.submit_decomposition").sort());

So a row that adds the two kinds to `PAYLOAD_KEYS` WITHOUT registering both handlers reds immediately. The vocabulary half and the registry half must land in ONE row. That is a measured fact, not a preference - re-check line 238 before disputing it.

WHAT CAN LAND ALONE IS THE FENCE, AND ONLY IN THIS DIRECTION. Excluding a kind that does not exist yet is a safe no-op, while registering a kind before excluding it is a SECURITY HOLE for the duration of a row. Measured at `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:84-90`: `WIRED_KINDS` is `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` FILTERED by `!MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS.includes(kind)`. A name in the exclusion roster that is absent from `PAYLOAD_KEYS` filters nothing and changes no served surface. `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` (`orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:195`) is a deny-set for the same reason. THEREFORE THIS ROW GOES FIRST and task-a2409cba depends on it - never the reverse.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: adding `environment.set_variable` and `environment.unset_variable` to `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` and to `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS`, plus the two test rosters that will otherwise red on the counts. NO vocabulary, NO PAYLOAD_KEYS, NO registry, NO handler, NO generated client - all of those are task-a2409cba.

- `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:60-83` - `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` is a frozen array of exactly SIX kinds: approval.decide, approval.decide_intent, product_contract.answer_clarification, cutover.activate, graph.approve, repository.publish. Each carries a comment giving its standing contract; follow that convention.
- `daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts:322-324` - TWO HARD COUNTS, `expect(expectedExclusions).toHaveLength(6)` and `expect(MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS).toHaveLength(6)`, plus a sorted set-equality against a locally transcribed list. Both become 8 and the list gains both kinds. This file is invisible to a grep for the new kind literals and is the single most likely thing to be missed.
- `orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:195-208` - `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS`, the ONE definition (`agent-wrapper.ts:24` re-exports it; do not look for a second).
- `grep -rln HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` -> exactly three files: agent-spawn-contract.ts, agent-wrapper.ts (re-export only), and `http/affordance-planning-offers.test.ts` (the only asserter). Check that last one for a count or an exact-roster arm before assuming it stays green.

THE HEADER OF mcp-tool-allowlist.ts CARRIES A STANDING CONTRACT about RE-ADMITTING kinds (removing them from the roster). This row only ADDS, which that contract permits and in fact anticipates. Do not read it as a bar on additions.

comments.author: worker-caece97b
comments.content:
THE ROW'S CENTRAL PREMISE IS REFUTED BY TWO COMMITTED INVARIANTS. I filed this row, planned it, and my own premise was wrong. Measured, not argued.

THE PREMISE I WROTE: "excluding a kind that does not exist yet is a safe no-op", because `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:92-98` computes `WIRED_KINDS` as `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` filtered by the exclusion roster, so a name absent from PAYLOAD_KEYS filters nothing.

THAT HALF IS TRUE AND I PROVED IT. After adding both kinds, `wiredMcpToolKinds()` was byte-identical to the step-1 before-value, COUNT=46 both sides. The served surface genuinely does not move.

BUT THE ROSTER IS NOT A DENY-LIST OF NAMES. It means "kinds that ARE wired but are NOT advertised", and two arms in `apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts` enforce exactly that, each with a comment saying why it exists:

  :101-113  "excludes kinds that are REAL vocabulary keys, and excludes them from the roster"
      for (const kind of MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS) {
        expect({ kind, real: vocabulary.includes(kind) }).toEqual({ kind, real: true });
      }
    Its comment: "A MISSPELLED member would exclude nothing and leave every other arm green, so the
    roster is pinned against the vocabulary it claims to subtract from."

  :244-257  "C2 keeps every excluded kind SERVED by the registry - this closes ONE transport"
      const served: readonly string[] = [...provider.provide().registry.keys()];
      for (const kind of MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS) {
        expect({ kind, served: served.includes(kind) }).toEqual({ kind, served: true });
      }
    Its comment: "the kinds leave the MCP ADVERTISEMENT and stay fully wired in the daemon... Without
    this arm, deleting them from PAYLOAD_KEYS outright would also pass C1."

A kind that does not exist in PAYLOAD_KEYS and is not in the registry fails BOTH. The very arm designed to catch a misspelling catches an unwired kind, because to that arm they are the same thing. Adding the fence early is indistinguishable from typing a name that will never exist - and that is the correct behaviour, not a defect to work around.

MEASURED, the full red set from `vitest run src/daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts src/mcp-main.test.ts src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.test.ts src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts`: `Test Files 3 failed | 1 passed (4)` / `Tests 7 failed | 47 passed (54)`.
  mcp-main.test.ts            STDIO-1 omits every excluded kind ... expected 8 to be 6
  mcp-http-host.test.ts       HTTP-1 refuses tools/call ...        expected 8 to be 6
  mcp-http-host.test.ts       HTTP-2 does not advertise ...        expected 8 to be 6
  mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts  pins an EXACT frozen denominator     expected 8 to be 6
  mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts  advertises far fewer kinds ...       expected 46 to be 44
  mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts  excludes kinds that are REAL ...     INVARIANT 1
  mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts  C2 keeps every excluded kind SERVED  INVARIANT 2

A SECOND PLANNING ERROR OF MINE, visible in that list. I wrote in planningNotes that "mcp-main.test.ts:216 and mcp-http-host.test.ts:658 all map over MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS itself" and therefore stay green. They DO map over it - and they ALSO carry their own hard `6`. I greped for the symbol, saw a `.map(...)`, and stopped. I never opened `src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts` at all, which is the file that actually owns the roster's semantics. Global rail 19 says to grep the SHAPE, not the symbol; I did the thing it warns against.

SO THE TRUE COST OF PUBLISHING THESE TWO KINDS IS ~17 FILES, not the 13 I measured: the four hard-count test files above are forced too, and they are welded to the registry wiring by invariant 2 exactly as `daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:238` welds PAYLOAD_KEYS to the registry.
